ash: Heads up — getting a flood of DCGM ECC/Xid alerts from us-west2-prod GPUs. ~30 alerts in the last hour, mostly single-sample Xid spikes. Anyone else seeing the noise?

kevin: Yep. Rule is currently firing on small increases to dcgm_xid_errors_total per scrape. We end up paging for transients that clear on the next scrape.

maya: Can we debounce at the Prometheus side by requiring a windowed aggregate and grouping by gpu_serial (not node name)? That avoids double counting across MIG slices.

jules: Agreed. Proposal: introduce a composite "gpu_card_degraded" signal that joins DCGM ECC, XID and NVML health metrics. Only alert when the aggregated signal is sustained (e.g., >0 across a 10–15m window) and when either multiple cards on the same node are affected or the same card shows repeated degradation.

kevin: Sketch of the alert expression I'm thinking (PromQL):

```
# recording rule: per-card error increases
gpu_card_xid_increase = sum by (gpu_serial) (increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[10m]))

gpu_card_ecc_increase = sum by (gpu_serial) (increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[10m]))

# composite alert expr (recording rules then alert):
(gpu_card_xid_increase > 0) or (gpu_card_ecc_increase > 0) or (max_over_time(nvml_gpu_health_status{job="nvml-exporter"}[10m]) > 0)
```
Alert rule example:

```
- alert: GPUCardDegraded
  expr: |
    sum by (gpu_serial) (
      increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[10m])
      + increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[10m])
    ) > 0
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    component: gpu
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU card {{ $labels.gpu_serial }} degraded (XID/ECC)"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-triage"
```

maya: A couple of implementation notes:
- Use recording rules (gpu_card_xid_increase / gpu_card_ecc_increase) so the alert rule stays readable and cheap.
- Group by gpu_serial and maybe gpu_uuid; avoid node-level grouping for MIG.
- Set initial severity to `info` in staging, then `warning` in prod if stable.

ash: We also need a drain/replacement decision matrix in the runbook. My suggestion: only auto-label node as `gpu:flaky` after 3 distinct card_degraded alerts for the same gpu_serial within 7d. Auto-drain only when `gpu:flaky` and node has >1 degraded card or if the card degradation coincides with pod-quality degradations. Otherwise flag for manual triage.

jules: Rollout plan:
1) Add recording rules + low-severity alert to staging (kevin).
2) Let it run 48h with alert metadata turned to info and create dashboards for gpu_card_xid_increase.
3) If noise drops >90% vs raw rule, promote to prod and bump to warning.
4) Add automated labeling (but not auto-drain) behind a flag.

oncall-bot: [automated] Silence created: GPUCardRawXidSpike in us-west2-prod for 1h by kevin to reduce alert churn while we test the new rules.

kevin: I'll open the PR with recording rules + sample alert. Also plan to add a small exporter-side smoothing option (dcgm-exporter: --debounce=5s) to avoid pathological scrape spikes.

maya: I'll update the runbook with the drain matrix and the label lifecycle (candidate -> flaky -> investigate). Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-triage

ash: Note on cost/ops: don't rush to replace hardware in region-constrained pools. If a single card is ephemeral-flaky, we prioritize workload migration and add node to maintenance pool rather than immediate RMA. Only escalate to hardware replacement for persistent ECC/XID frequency or for cards that fail NVML health checks.

jules: One more: add a Prometheus recording rule that counts distinct gpu_serials with degradation over 24h; use that metric to drive capacity planning and alert when >X cards degraded in a region.

kevin: Action items: kevin -> PR with rules + test dashboard; maya -> runbook edits; ash -> mark candidate nodes and help triage; jules -> follow up on capacity alert.

ash: :thumbsup: Thanks all — will watch the staging results and post back.

kevin: PR posted to eng-infra/staging in ~30m. Will paste link here when ready. :+1:

maya: thanks, will review and add runbook patch.

jules: good plan. If noise reduction is solid we can retire old raw alerts after 72h of stable behavior.
